43.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
43.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

44.meaning: And others — additional ones, different persons besides those already mentioned. The base word means 'others/other ones', here in the masculine plural with the connector 'and'.
44.grammar: A noun/adjective 'other(s)' in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending is the sound masculine plural in the subject/nominative form — marking it as the subject or as something simply named. The opening wa is 'and'.
44.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being later, an 'other', the remaining

45.meaning: 'They fight' or 'they do battle' — engaging in mutual combat or warfare. The pattern (qātala) conveys fighting against an opponent, a reciprocal struggle rather than mere striking.
45.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb in the mutual-action pattern (fā'ala) meaning 'to fight against'. The -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural 'they' subject and the indicative mood, which states an action as an ongoing or habitual fact.

46.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
46.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

47.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
47.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

48.meaning: The proper name of the One True God in Arabic — Allah, the unique, supreme Deity worshipped alone, without partner or equal. It is a name, not a common noun, and is not pluralized or made feminine.
48.grammar: The divine proper name. The final '-i' (kasra) is the genitive case — the case taken after a preposition or when the name is linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah'). Being a name, it carries no indefinite tanwīn.
48.root: — (the divine proper name; not derived from a triliteral root in the ordinary sense)

49.meaning: So recite — an imperative commanding recitation; qara'a in Arabic means both to read aloud and to recite from memory. The fa- at the front signals a consequential link: 'therefore, do this as a result of what was just said'.

parts.en: recite! (imperative plural stem with -ū plural marker)
silent alif fariqah — a purely orthographic convention written after the waw of plural verb forms; never pronounced

49.grammar: The base verb is qara'a (Form I). The imperative plural (amr for the 2nd person masculine plural) is formed with the -ū (waw) ending, which is the actual plural marker. The hamzat al-waṣl (alif at the start of the imperative) is a connecting hamza required because the imperative stem begins with a sukūn; it drops in pronunciation when preceded by fa-. The final alif is the alif fariqah — a silent orthographic convention written after the waw of masculine plural verb forms and never pronounced. It has no phonetic value and does not represent a vowel.
49.root: ق-ر-أ (q-r-ʾ) — to read, to recite; the root from which 'Qur'an' derives

50.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
50.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

51.meaning: Was made easy, became easy — tayassara describes something becoming or being rendered accessible, manageable, or unburdensome. The Form V pattern conveys a reflexive or resultant ease: the thing came to be in a state of easiness, or was made easy.

parts.en: became easy / was made easy (Form V perfect stem from y-s-r)

51.grammar: This is a Form V (tafaʿʿala pattern) perfect (māḍī) verb. Form V is the reflexive/resultative counterpart of Form II: where Form II means 'to make easy', Form V means 'to become easy' or 'to find something easy for oneself'. The ta- prefix is part of the Form V morphological pattern (not a subject prefix). The -a ending is the 3rd person masculine singular perfect ending. In context it often translates as 'whatever is easy' or 'whatever has been made easy'.
51.root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — ease, facility; Form V: to become easy, to be facilitated

52.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
52.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
52.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

53.meaning: And establish / set up / perform fully — a command to make something stand firm and upright, to carry it out properly and consistently (used especially of performing prayer rightly).
53.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') joined to a plural command verb of the causative (af'ala) pattern, meaning to make something stand/be upright. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural addressee being told to do it.
53.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright; to establish

54.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
54.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

55.meaning: And give / hand over / bring — a command to deliver something to someone, to render it to its due recipient.
55.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') joined to a plural command verb of the causative (af'ala) pattern, meaning to make something come to someone, i.e. to give. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural addressee being told to give.
55.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to give, bring

56.meaning: The purifying alms (zakāt) — the obligatory portion given from one's wealth that purifies it and causes it to grow; an act of worship and social due.
56.grammar: A definite feminine noun (the tied tā' marks the feminine). The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the alms').
56.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure; to grow, increase, be blessed

57.meaning: And give a goodly loan — aqriḍū commands giving a loan (qarḍ), specifically the loan of wealth to Allah (i.e., spending in His cause), with the expectation of generous repayment. The Qur'an uses this as a metaphor for charitable giving: what one gives sincerely is a 'loan' to Allah that He returns multiplied.

parts.en: give a loan! / lend! (Form IV imperative plural stem)
silent alif fariqah — a purely orthographic convention written after the waw of plural verb forms; never pronounced

57.grammar: The verb is Form IV (afʿala pattern) of the root q-r-ḍ: aqraḍa means 'to lend, to give a loan'. The imperative plural (2nd masculine plural command) is formed using the plural ending -ū (waw). The initial hamza of Form IV (aqraḍa) is hamzat al-qaṭʿ — a true, invariably-pronounced hamza, not hamzat al-waṣl; it is always pronounced regardless of what precedes it. The final alif is the silent alif fariqah, a purely graphic convention written after the waw of masculine plural verb forms and never pronounced. The wa- joins this command to what preceded.
57.root: ق-ر-ض (q-r-ḍ) — to lend, to give a loan; qarḍ = loan given in anticipation of return

58.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
58.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

59.meaning: A loan; something handed over to another to be repaid or given back later. It is the noun naming the act or object of lending.
59.grammar: The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n for indefiniteness, 'a loan'). The accusative is the case for the object of a verb, so this names what is being given or lent.

60.meaning: Good, fine, beautiful, excellent — pleasing and praiseworthy in quality. It describes something done well or possessing goodness and beauty.
60.grammar: An adjective ('good'). The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite). As an adjective it agrees with and describes a noun; the accusative case matches a noun in that same case.

61.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
61.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

62.meaning: You (plural) put forward, send ahead, or advance (something) — to send something on ahead of oneself, especially good deeds laid up for the future.
62.grammar: A present/imperfect verb addressed to a group of males. The tu- prefix marks 'you', and the -ū subject-ending (here shortened from -ūna) makes it plural ('you all'). The dropped final -n and the silent alif show the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive after a governing particle (e.g. 'that you send forward', 'whatever you send forward'). The doubled middle root letter (form II) gives a causative, deliberate sense: 'put forward'.
62.root: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — to precede, go ahead, advance

63.meaning: For yourselves / for your own selves — the preposition li- ('for, to') with the plural noun anfus ('selves, souls') and the pronoun 'your', conveying benefit accruing to one's own persons.
63.grammar: The preposition li- ('for/to') governs the noun anfus, which therefore takes the genitive -i ending; the possessive pronoun -kum ('your', plural) is attached. The genitive is required because the noun follows the preposition li-.
63.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

64.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
64.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

65.meaning: Good / goodness; also 'better' or 'best'. A word for what is good, beneficial, or excellent — and, by its pattern, often 'better than'.
65.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective ('good' or 'better'). The final -in (nunation with -i) marks it as indefinite ('some good / any good') and in the genitive case, typically after a preposition or in a possessive link.
65.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, what is better

66.meaning: You (plural) find it — to come upon, discover, or experience something as being a certain way. It carries an attached object pronoun 'it'.
66.grammar: A present/imperfect verb addressed to a group of males ('you all find'). The ta- prefix marks 'you' and the -ū ending marks a plural subject; the dropped final -n shows the verb stands in the subjunctive/jussive after a governing particle. The attached -hu is the object 'it/him': 'you will find IT'.
66.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, perceive

67.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
67.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

68.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
68.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

69.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
69.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

70.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
70.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

71.meaning: And greater — aʿẓam is the elative form (ism al-tafḍīl) meaning 'greater' or 'greatest' in terms of magnitude, importance, or significance. It is derived from ʿaẓuma ('to be great/mighty') and conveys a higher or highest degree of greatness.

parts.en: and (with emphatic doubling of the waw in connected speech)

71.grammar: aʿẓama is on the afʿal (أَفْعَل) pattern, which in Arabic forms the elative (ism al-tafḍīl) — a derived nominal category serving both 'greater than' (comparative) and 'the greatest' (superlative) depending on context. This is a nominal derived form, not a verbal Form IV, despite the superficial resemblance of the pattern. As a diptote (ghayr munsarif), it does not take tanwīn, and its accusative and genitive cases both surface as -a rather than -an/-in. The -a here is therefore the accusative/genitive case ending of a diptote noun, not merely a pattern filler. The wa- (written with shaddah on the waw in Arabic orthography) is the conjunction 'and', linking aʿẓama to a parallel word before it.
71.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — greatness, magnitude, might; elative ism al-tafḍīl: aʿẓam = greater/greatest

72.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
72.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
72.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

73.meaning: A call to 'seek forgiveness' — to ask Allah to forgive and cover over one's sins. The Form X pattern conveys actively requesting pardon, joined to a preceding clause by 'and'.
73.grammar: A plural command (imperative) verb, Form X (the ista- pattern, which means 'to seek/ask for' the base action — here 'to seek forgiveness'). The plural wāw (-ū) means 'you (plural masculine), do it!'. The prefixed wa- means 'and'. So: 'and seek forgiveness, all of you'.
73.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, cover over, pardon

74.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
74.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

75.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
75.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

76.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
76.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

77.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
77.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

78.meaning: Most Merciful / ever-compassionate — one whose mercy is deep, constant, and abundantly bestowed; an intensive form stressing enduring tenderness and care. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
78.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a lasting, abundant quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is most merciful").
